title: Pooled packet dots keep the previous packet's class material on slot reuse
evidence:
if used < pool.size():
	dot = pool[used]
	dot.visible = true
else:
	dot = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = DOT_RADIUS
	sphere.height = DOT_RADIUS * 2.0
	sphere.radial_segments = 10
	sphere.rings = 6
	dot.mesh = sphere
	dot.material_override = _dot_mats[pkt.cls]
detail: Dots are assigned to slots by position (`used`), but inflight composition changes every tick: a slot freed by a delivered email packet and refilled by a streaming packet keeps the yellow email material. Class color mislabels packets continuously during play.
recommended_fix: In the reuse branch, rebind the material each frame: after `dot = pool[used]`, also set `dot.material_override = _dot_mats[pkt.cls]` (cheap dictionary lookup per dot).

title: Zoom/magnify during a held pipe press keeps SELECT alive; release opens the pre-zoom pick
evidence:
_picked_pipe = flow_view.pick_pipe(screen_pos, camera)
_mode = Mode.SELECT if _picked_pipe >= 0 else Mode.ORBIT
...
	if was == Mode.SELECT and _picked_pipe >= 0 \
			and screen_pos.distance_to(_press_pos) <= CLICK_SLOP_PX:
		pipe_selected.emit(_picked_pipe)
detail: Wheel/magnify zoom moves the camera while the button is held without converting SELECT to ORBIT (only mouse-motion events check the slop). The pointer stays within slop, so release selects the pipe hit by the press-time camera, not the one now under the cursor.
recommended_fix: On zoom_requested while _mode == Mode.SELECT, either convert to ORBIT like the motion-slop path or re-run pick_pipe against the updated camera before emitting pipe_selected.

title: Editor shot dereferences get_camera_3d() without a null check
detail: vp3d is guarded, but SubViewport.get_camera_3d() returns null when no camera is active in that viewport; the harness then crashes on cam.global_transform instead of falling back to the window viewport.
recommended_fix: Guard the camera too: `if vp3d != null and vp3d.get_camera_3d() != null:` before moving it, letting the existing window-viewport fallback handle the no-camera editor state.
